title: backlog.py ops SP prints a sprint's operational rows
goal: A read-only backlog.py ops SP (a bl_ops module behind the backlog.py facade, reusing bl_stall.ops_rows) prints, as text, from the spool and the committed ops sidecars, the rows that name one of the sprint's items: land.end and land.step per item, done.refused with its reasons, and agent.run (a worker's run is one; the group is the agent type), and nothing of an item outside the sprint or of a row with no item; an id the backlog does not hold is refused, exit 2; tools.md and backlog.md list it.

run:
import os,sys,json,subprocess as sp,tempfile,shutil
from pathlib import Path
t=Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
os.environ["CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA"]=str(t/"d")
os.environ["CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT"]=str(Path.cwd())
sys.path.insert(0,"_tools")
import ql_capture as q
b=t/"r/kb/_self/backlog"
b.mkdir(parents=True)
it=lambda i,k,**kw:(b/(i+".json")).write_text(json.dumps({"id":i,"kind":k,"title":"t "+i,"status":"done","goal":"g","priority":"P3","rank":0,**kw}))
it("SP-aaaaaaaa","sprint",status="active")
it("ST-bbbbbbbb","story",sprint="SP-aaaaaaaa")
it("ST-cccccccc","story",sprint="SP-aaaaaaaa")
it("ST-dddddddd","story")
q.record("ops",event="land.end",item="ST-bbbbbbbb",exit=0,ms=5)
q.record("ops",event="land.step",item="ST-bbbbbbbb",step="rebase",exit=0,ms=5)
q.record("ops",event="done.refused",item="ST-cccccccc",reasons=["check-failed"],ms=5)
q.record("ops",event="agent.run",item="ST-bbbbbbbb",group="kbworker",ms=5)
q.record("ops",event="agent.run",group="nonitem",ms=5)
q.record("ops",event="land.end",item="ST-dddddddd",exit=0,ms=5)
q.record("ops",event="land.step",item="ST-dddddddd",step="outsider",exit=0,ms=5)
r=sp.run([sys.executable,"_tools/backlog.py","--root",str(t/"r"),"ops","SP-aaaaaaaa"],capture_output=True,text=True)
shutil.rmtree(t)
o=r.stdout
ok=r.returncode==0 and all(w in o for w in ("land.end","land.step","rebase","done.refused","check-failed","agent.run","kbworker","ST-bbbbbbbb","ST-cccccccc")) and not any(w in o for w in ("ST-dddddddd","outsider","nonitem"))
print("ops rc",r.returncode,"stdout lines",len(o.splitlines()),"stderr",r.stderr.strip()[-60:])
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

import subprocess as s,sys,tempfile,os,shutil
t=tempfile.mkdtemp()
s.run(["git","init","-q",t],check=True)
os.makedirs(t+"/kb/_self/backlog")
r=s.run([sys.executable,os.getcwd()+"/_tools/backlog.py","--root",t,"ops","SP-zzzzzzzz"],capture_output=True,text=True,cwd=t)
shutil.rmtree(t,ignore_errors=True)
out=r.stdout+r.stderr
print("ops of an unknown sprint: exit",r.returncode,out.strip()[-120:])
sys.exit(0 if r.returncode==2 and "SP-zzzzzzzz" in out and "invalid choice" not in out else 1)

import re,sys
miss=[p for p in ("kb/_self/tools.md","kb/_self/backlog.md") if not re.search(r"backlog\.py ops\b",open(p,encoding="utf-8").read())]
print("docs without backlog.py ops:",miss)
sys.exit(1 if miss else 0)

gates.question: What does backlog.py ops SP do for a sprint id the backlog no longer holds (a closed sprint, deleted with its items)?
options: refuse it as any unknown id: exit 2 naming the id
read the sprint's items back from git history as cost does
gates.recommendation: refuse it as any unknown id: exit 2 naming the id
gates.answer: refuse it as any unknown id: exit 2 naming the id

gates.question: Does backlog.py ops print a --json form beside its text, as stalled does?
Does backlog.py ops SP print a row that names no item (an agent.run of a subagent with no item, sync.gate, test.run), or only rows that name one of the sprint's items?
options: only rows that name one of the sprint's items
gates.recommendation: only rows that name one of the sprint's items
gates.answer: only rows that name one of the sprint's items

notes: Premise: backlog.py ops is an invalid choice (exit 2). .claude/settings.json already allows Bash(python3 _tools/backlog.py *). A closed sprint's items come from git history as bl_cost restores them; the check plants an open sprint only. Backlog triage 2026-10-10: its dependency ST-fd33riif “The committed ops sidecars hold no fixture landing” was dropped; the ops reader filters rows by the sprint's own items, so fixture rows in past sidecars do not reach it. Premise run 2026-10-10: backlog.py ops SP is 'invalid choice' (exit 2), reproduces. The goal named worker.run, which is no event of ql_capture.OPS_EVENTS: a worker's run is an agent.run row, so the goal says so; the rows of a spool and a sidecar are read by bl_stall.ops_rows (agent.run rows of a closed session come from the sidecar, land and done rows from the spool too).
